record.paper_title: On some open problems related to the restricted Burnside problem.
record.original_question: Fix positive integers m and n, let F_m be the free group on m generators, and call an element of F_m primitive if it belongs to some free generating set of F_m. Suppose G is an m-generated finite group, residually finite group, or profinite group with a chosen generating m-tuple such that the periodicity condition x^n = 1 is imposed only on the values of primitive words on those generators, rather than on all elements of G. Must G then be soluble-by-finite, with bounds depending only on m and n for both the derived length and the index of a soluble subgroup?

evidence.quote: In Section 1 several problems are discussed in which the periodicity condition x^n=1 is imposed not on all but only on some elements of an m-generated finite (or residually finite, or profinite) group, for example, on the values on the fixed m generators of the so-called primitive elements of the free group F_m. (An element of F_m is said to be primitive if it can be included into a system of free generators of F_m.) The group is then conjectured to be soluble-by-finite, with bounds in terms of m and n for the derived length and the index of a soluble subgroup.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m, n$ be fixed positive integers. Let $F_m$ denote the free group on $m$ free generators $x_1, \dots, x_m$. An element $w \in F_m$ is called primitive if it belongs to some free generating set of $F_m$ (equivalently, $w$ is the image of $x_1$ under some automorphism of $F_m$). 

Let $G$ be a group equipped with an ordered generating $m$-tuple $(g_1, \dots, g_m)$, and assume $G$ is either a finite group, a residually finite group, or a profinite group (in the profinite case the tuple is required to generate $G$ topologically). For every primitive element $w \in F_m$, impose the relation
$$w(g_1, \dots, g_m)^n = 1.$$

Note that this relation is imposed only on values of primitive words, not on all elements of $G$.

Question: Must $G$ be soluble-by-finite? More precisely, do there exist functions $d = d(m,n)$ and $i = i(m,n)$, depending only on $m$ and $n$, such that $G$ contains a soluble normal subgroup of derived length at most $d(m,n)$ and index at most $i(m,n)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is presented as a conjecture in the context of variants of the restricted Burnside problem, where periodicity is imposed only on primitive-word values rather than all elements. While Zelmanov solved the classical restricted Burnside problem (1989–91), the primitive-word variant asking for soluble-by-finite structure with bounds depending on m and n appears to remain open; no resolution was located in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Burnside problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Zelmanov solved the restricted Burnside problem for arbitrary exponent (1989-91); variants where the exponent condition is imposed on restricted families of elements are discussed as separate problems.
status_evidence.claim: The classical restricted Burnside problem is solved, but the primitive-word variant is a distinct open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The Burnside problem and related topics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Burnside-type problems and related open questions including periodicity conditions on selected elements.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys consider such restricted-periodicity problems as still-open conjectures.
